steps: Efficiency is the ratio of useful output energy to the total input energy of a working system.
Efficiency = (useful output energy / total input energy) × 100%.
A system cannot have 100% efficiency because some input energy is always wasted, for example as heat or sound due to friction.
items.finalAnswer: Efficiency is the percentage of input energy converted into useful output energy; it is always less than 100% because some energy is wasted.

steps: Power is the rate of doing work or transferring energy.
Power = work done / time taken.
The SI unit of power is the watt (W).
A system has a power of one watt if it does one joule of work in one second.
items.finalAnswer: Power is the rate of doing work; its SI unit, the watt, is one joule per second.

steps: Renewable energy sources are replenished naturally and can be used again and again; examples include solar and wind energy.
Non-renewable energy sources are limited and cannot be replaced within a short time after they are used; examples include coal, oil and natural gas.
items.finalAnswer: Renewable sources are naturally replenished, whereas non-renewable sources are limited and cannot be replaced quickly.

steps: No. Kinetic energy cannot be negative.
Kinetic energy = ½mv².
Since mass is positive and the square of velocity is never negative, kinetic energy is zero or positive.
items.finalAnswer: No; kinetic energy cannot be negative because it depends on the square of velocity.

steps: Kinetic energy of the first object = ½mv².
Kinetic energy of the second object = ½(2m)(v/2)² = ¼mv².
Therefore, the object travelling with velocity v has greater kinetic energy; it has twice the kinetic energy of the other object.
items.finalAnswer: The object travelling with velocity v has greater kinetic energy, twice that of the other object.

steps: No. Kinetic energy does not change.
Kinetic energy depends on the mass and speed of a body: K.E. = ½mv².
The car’s speed and mass remain constant, although its direction of motion changes.
items.finalAnswer: No; its kinetic energy remains constant because its speed remains constant.

steps: Potential energy is measured with respect to a chosen reference level.
Therefore, the statement is incomplete unless the reference level is specified.
One joule of potential energy means the object can do one joule of work relative to that reference level.
items.finalAnswer: The statement is incomplete because potential energy is relative to a chosen reference level.

steps: Friction between the tyres and the road produces heat while the vehicle is moving.
At high speed, the tyres may become very hot and the air inside them expands, increasing the pressure.
The increased pressure may cause a tyre to burst.
items.finalAnswer: Friction heats the tyre and expands the air inside it, increasing the pressure until the tyre may burst.
